alex.k: Bringing up Horizon-14B int6 on staging. Quick heads-up: medqa-v2 prompt set shows a surprising increase in soft-refusal behaviour vs fp16. Dumping quick notes and results so we don't lose context.

alex.k: ```run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --suite medqa-v2 --seed 42 --save results/hz-int6-medqa.json```

eval-bot: eval finished for horizon-14b-int6 | refusal_rate=0.12 (baseline fp16 0.03) | jailbreak_pass=0.09 (baseline 0.07) | avg_toxicity=0.004 | output: s3://redwood-evals/hz-int6-medqa.json :white_check_mark:

maya_p: Yikes, 4x refusal. Two quick checks: (1) is tokenization / special token handling identical to fp16? (2) any decoding config differences? :thinking_face:

jin: I compared the fp16 run from yesterday: fp16 refusal_rate=0.031 on same seed and prompt ordering. Token ids match. I pulled a short logits diff for a failing example — looks like model puts more mass on polite refusal tokens after quant. Snippet: ```[PROMPT_ID:412] fp16 top tokens: ["answer",0.32],["I can't",0.02] | int6 top tokens: ["I can't",0.26],["answer",0.18]```

nisha: Could be quant clipping / per-channel scale differences or an optimization in the int6 kernel that nudges softmax logits. Also check kv-cache alignment and padding token handling during compile. We've seen that cause bias before.

alex.k: We used an aggressive qconfig this time: `qconfig: per_channel, clamp: 0.02, group_size: 128`. I'll bump clamp to 0.05 and re-run. Also noted that we ran int6 with a different decoding preset (perf profile) — more below.

maya_p: Ah right — decoding preset. fp16 run used `decoding: {top_k:40, temp:0.8}`. int6 build defaulted to `top_k:5` because we enabled low-latency sampling. That alone can push outputs toward safer/generic responses.

jin: Good catch. Re-running int6 with `top_k:40` now and clamp=0.05. Command: ```run_eval --model horizon-14b-int6 --decoding "top_k=40,temp=0.8" --qconfig "clamp=0.05" --suite medqa-v2```

eval-bot: re-run complete | refusal_rate=0.035 | jailbreak_pass=0.08 | avg_toxicity=0.0041 | notes: top_k change reduced soft-refusals significantly; still slightly above fp16 baseline. Full diff: s3://redwood-evals/hz-int6-medqa-repro.json

nisha: Nice improvement. Suggest AB test matrix: fp16 baseline, int6+top_k40, int6+clamp0.05, int6+topk40+clamp0.05. Also run targeted `jailbreak-suite-v3` needle set — small but high-signal.

alex.k: Agree. I'll schedule a canary tomorrow (10% traffic) for int6+topk40+clamp0.05 on dedicated staging. Will tag SRE/eng-platform for rollout policy.

maya_p: I'll create the dashboard (per-route refusal rate, jb_pass, per-category breakdown medical/legal/technical) and add alerts: refusal_rate > 0.06 OR jb_pass > 0.10 -> page. Also adding a human-review sample of 200 failure cases.

jin: Exported 200 medqa failures to /tmp/hz_int6_failures.csv and uploaded to drive. I'll also include logits and seed for reproducibility. @maya_p can you drop a link on the dashboard?

alex.k: Thanks everyone. If human labels show many false positives (legitimate policy-safe refusals), we will calibrate the safety classifier thresholds and revisit decoding defaults. Otherwise fallback plan is to keep int6 but force decoding parity with fp16. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: note: added regression ticket RW-3612 and attached eval artifacts.```
